note: Each control breaks one named safety invariant in a copy of the source and expects at least one of the listed JVM tests to FAIL. A control that survives is a witness gap, not a pass. Run locally with tools/invariant_controls.py; never commit a mutated file. Controls whose mutation is masked by a second, redundant guard (equivalent mutants, e.g. '..' and absolute ZIP paths are also refused by the blank-segment and trailing-dot rules) are not kept. Tier limit (2026-11-26): the Local Add enablement conditions in LocalEngineScreen used to survive every JVM control because the JVM harness always satisfied them; they now live in the pure LocalAddAvailability with a witness per condition, but the composable's wiring of the facts into it is witnessed only by installed journeys. Defensive-only branches that no reachable scenario can drive (e.g. the RemoteUniversalAddAdapter catch that maps a failure after the load boundary to a refusal-or-rethrow: RTorrentRemote already converts every post-dispatch failure to Uncertain) are pinned by a behavior test but not kept as controls. Seed-copy exclusivity (CREATE_NEW) and free-space refusal survive the JVM tests (the acquisition-race test hooks a different layer; free space cannot be forced); both remain witnessed only by the real-engine and installed journeys. The ticket/opt-out checks in RemoteCredentialLock.saveVerifiedPairIfCurrent are repeated inside the roster and vault saves, so removing the outer one is an equivalent mutant; the behavior is pinned by RememberedLoginPersistenceTest.
